# Urological procedures postop antimicrobial prophylaxis:

*Postoperative antimicrobial administration for preventing SSI is not necessary for most procedures.

*Prophylactic antibiotics should be discontinued within 24 hours.

<Click here> AUA Surgery Abx Prophylaxis Guidelines

References

- MVAHCS Urology Section (July 2023)
- Lightner DJ, et al. Best Practice Statement on Urologic Procedures and Antimicrobial Prophylaxis, J Urol (2020) 203:351
- Bratzler DW, et al.  Clinical practice guidelines for antimicrobial prophy in surgery, Am J Health-Syst Pharm. 2013 Vol 70 page 195-283
Therapy:
## INPATIENT Postop IV medications:

Preferred:

[Cefazolin Weight Based Dosing q8h x2 doses postop](surg-cefazolin-wt-based-postop-doses-x2)

Alternative for beta lactam allergy:

Click here Beta-lactam allergy assessment

[Vancomycin 15mg/kg Dosing q12h x1 dose postop](surg-vancomycin-post-op-specific-dosing)

## INPATIENT Postop Oral Medications:

Cephalexin 500mg PO q6h X1 day postop urology ($) R

< OR >
Sulfa/Trimeth DS 1 tablet po q12h X1 day postop urology procedure ($) R,DI

< OR >
Nitrofurantoin SA 1 capsule q12h X1 day postop urology procedure ($) R,O

## OUTPATIENT POSTOP PRESCRIPTION ORDERS:

Prophylaxis may be recommended in limited cases due to the severity of
complications of postoperative infection (e.g., an infected device that is
not easily removable).

Cephalexin 500mg PO qid X5 days postop urology procedure ($) R

< OR >
Sulfa/Trimeth 1 DS tablet PO q12h X5 days postop urology procedure ($) R,DI

< OR >
Nitrofurantoin SA 1 capsule q12h X5 days postop urology procedure ($) R,O
